newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed ahead of report.

text.p: Evening up ahead of the Cattle-on-Feed report kept trade uneven and CME live cattle futures closed mixed. Feeder cattle held gains as cash expectations offset higher corn futures prices, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.200 cent higher to 0.050 lower with June up most at 64.475 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.050 to 0.275 higher with May up the least at 70.900 cents.
Short covering supported live cattle futures much of the morning despite lower cash beef prices, then late positioning ahead of the report made for a mixed trend going into the close, traders said.

Estimates for seven-state major feedlots on feed averaged 107.6 percent and ranged from 106 to 108 percent of last year. Placements averaged 103.3 percent and ranged from 100.5 to 107 percent and marketings averaged 100.6 percent and ranged from 98 to 104.5 percent.

Smith Barney, RBH and R.J. O'Brien lightly sold June against mixed commission house buying early. In live cattle options, there was small put buying early and a June 60/63 put spread, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle showed support despite higher grain futures. Strength continued to stem from concern over death losses in the Dakotas from the recent blizzard and the outlook for tighter feeder supplies ahead, traders said.
Refco, Smith Barney and R.J. O'Brien were light buyers while locals sold early, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.11 at $70.48 per cwt.
